chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a small thing falls into the well and dies in it, then draw out buckets from it. If a person in janabah falls into it, then draw out seven buckets from it. And if a camel dies in it, or wine is poured into it, then all of the water must be drawn out.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَاءُ كُلُّهُ: all of the well water, which must be removed in the stated cases
key_terms.بَعِيرٌ: a camel whose death in the well necessitates a stricter ruling
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: wine, whose presence causes severe contamination
key_terms.سَبْعَ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets to be drawn from the well
key_terms.شَيْءٌ صَغِيرٌ: a small creature or small thing falling into the well and dying in it

ai.seo_question: What should be done if an animal dies in a well or wine is poured into it according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the contamination of well water by different causes. It distinguishes between lesser and greater forms of impurity, assigning partial removal of water in some cases and complete drainage in more severe cases.
